name: 5558-batchdecode-dsv2lite-tp8
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite. ~30 GB of bf16 safetensors, ungated, already in the local HF cache.
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3 of one node, NV18 all-to-all NVLink.
parallelism: TP=8 with data-parallel attention over DP=4: four data-parallel groups of two tensor-parallel ranks. Attention runs per group over that group's own requests; the MoE and dense FFN are tensor-parallel over all eight ranks. No expert and no pipeline parallelism.
architecture: DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, 15.7B total / 2.4B active per token, bf16: 27 decoder layers of which 26 are MoE (64 routed experts, 6 per token, plus 2 shared), MLA attention with 16 heads.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=512, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 1536 requests with a 3600 s safety cap. The global admission cap is 512 as well, so each of the four groups holds ~128 requests.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix and no shared structure: exactly 512 prompt tokens in and 512 out, both stdev 0, temperature 0.0 and ignore_eos true. The radix cache is off.
purpose: A mixture-of-experts chat assistant generating 512-token replies for 512 concurrent users on eight GPUs.
launch:
# sglang launch arguments, `sglang serve` CLI form: one `key: value` per line. An indented or
# nested block is skipped silently, so every value must stay on the one line it is written on.

model-path: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite

# The checkpoint ships its own configuration and modeling modules.
trust-remote-code: true

tp-size: 8
dp-size: 4
enable-dp-attention: true

# LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC: the checkpoint advertises 163840 positions and the engine sizes a
# device-side int32 req_to_token table of (max requests + 1) x (context length + 4) from that
# number, which at the advertised window is hundreds of gigabytes and the server never starts.
# 4096 is the checkpoint's own pre-YaRN window; the longest request here is 512 + 512 = 1024.
context-length: 4096

# GLOBAL, and the engine divides it by dp-size: 512 here is 128 admitted per data-parallel group.
max-running-requests: 512

disable-radix-cache: true

# 0.80 rather than the engine's derived 0.81 for tp>=8, to leave room to capture CUDA graphs at a
# global batch of 512.
mem-fraction-static: 0.80

# PINNED, and not decoration: the default capture ladder stops at 160 and `--cuda-graph-max-bs`
# only trims that list, it cannot extend it; and under data-parallel attention the graph is
# selected on the GLOBAL token count across all four groups. Without this list a 512-request batch
# matches no graph and runs eager, with no error and no log line. Keep it on ONE line.
cuda-graph-bs: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 288, 320, 352, 384, 416, 448, 480, 512]

random-seed: 42
